text: {"memo": "Apple Inc. (AAPL) delivered another strong performance in FY2024, capping a multi-year streak of resilient growth despite macroeconomic headwinds. Revenue reached $383 billion, up 3% year-over-year, marking the third consecutive year of growth after the pandemic-era pullback in FY2022. Services revenue continued to be a key driver, growing 14% to $85 billion, while iPhone sales stabilized at $200 billion, reflecting strong upgrade cycles and robust demand in emerging markets. The Mac and iPad segments remained under pressure, declining 3% and 2%, respectively, as post-pandemic demand normalized. Gross margin expanded to 29.3%, up 120 basis points, driven by favorable product mix and cost efficiencies, while operating margin improved to 30.3%. Net income rose 6% to $97 billion, translating to diluted EPS of $6.16, a 7% increase. Free cash flow remained robust at $110 billion, supporting Apple’s aggressive capital return program, including $90 billion in share repurchases and $14 billion in dividends during the year. Over the past five years (FY2020-FY2024), revenue has grown at a 6% CAGR, with services and wearables emerging as high-margin growth engines. The company’s balance sheet remains pristine, with $166 billion in net cash. While near-term iPhone growth may moderate, Apple’s ecosystem strength, pricing power, and AI-driven innovation (e.g., on-device AI features in iOS 18) position it well for long-term resilience. The stock remains a core holding for growth and stability."}
